backlog.spec: Leave the model untouched and post-process the predictions. For each test molecule compute its maximum Tanimoto similarity s to any training molecule, using binary Morgan fingerprints (radius 2, 2048 bits). Map s to a trust weight w = clip((s - 0.2) / 0.3, 0, 1), so molecules with max similarity at or below 0.2 are fully distrusted and those at or above 0.5 are fully trusted. Return w * pred + (1 - w) * m, where pred is the current pipeline's prediction and m is the median of train_y. Compute the fingerprints once per molecule with the existing caching style. Because every fold tests on unseen scaffolds, some test molecules are far from the training set, and for MAE it is better to fall back toward the median than to trust a confident extrapolation.
backlog.title: Similarity-gated shrinkage toward the training median

backlog.spec: Extend featurize_one so the cached vector concatenates four pieces: the current Morgan count fingerprint, the current RDKit descriptor block, the 167 MACCS keys (from rdkit.Chem.MACCSkeys.GenMACCSKeys, converted to a float32 array), and a 1024-length atom-pair count fingerprint from rdFingerprintGenerator.GetAtomPairGenerator(fpSize=1024).GetCountFingerprintAsNumPy. Leave fit_predict and all model hyperparameters unchanged. The aim is to supply substructure-key and topological-distance information that Morgan radius 2 does not encode.
backlog.title: Add MACCS keys and atom-pair counts to the features

backlog.spec: Pick the stage-2 boosting budget per fold instead of hard-coding 400. Inside fit_predict, after computing the ridge base and the feature matrix, run a 4-fold GroupKFold over the training molecules grouped by Murcko scaffold (rdkit.Chem.Scaffolds.MurckoScaffold.MurckoScaffoldSmiles, falling back to the SMILES itself if it fails). For each inner fold, fit the same two-stage model on the inner-train part and evaluate inner-validation MAE at stage-2 round counts in {100, 200, 400, 700, 1000} using the booster's iteration_range / ntree_limit so one fit covers all candidates. Average the MAE curves across the four inner folds, pick the best round count, then refit the two-stage model on the full training set with that many stage-2 rounds and predict. Keep features, ridge base and all tree hyperparameters unchanged.
backlog.title: Choose the number of L1 rounds by inner scaffold-grouped CV

backlog.spec: Generalise featurize so it takes a radius argument and builds a separate cached feature matrix per radius, each being the Morgan count fingerprint at that radius concatenated with the usual RDKit descriptor block. In fit_predict, run the complete existing residual-boosting procedure three times, once on the radius-1 matrix, once on radius 2 and once on radius 3, and return base_te plus the mean of the three residual predictions. The shared Ridge baseline is computed once. Different radii capture different substructure scales and their errors should partially cancel.
backlog.title: Average predictions over several Morgan radii

backlog.spec: In the current two-stage residual model, replace the stage-2 objective reg:absoluteerror with XGBoost's built-in reg:pseudohubererror and set huber_slope=0.3 (roughly a third of the target's spread, so most residuals are in the quadratic regime and only the tails are down-weighted). Keep stage 1 as 200 rounds of reg:squarederror and keep stage 2 continuing from stage 1's booster with the same 400 rounds and the same tree hyperparameters (max_depth=6, learning_rate=0.03, subsample=0.8, colsample_bytree=0.3, min_child_weight=3). Everything else, including the physchem ridge base and the features, stays as is. The aim is a smoother gradient than pure L1 while still being robust, which should help MAE on a 728-row dataset where the L1 gradient is piecewise constant and uninformative.
backlog.title: Pseudo-Huber loss for the second boosting stage

backlog.spec: Keep the current two-stage model but, instead of using only the final booster, average predictions from several snapshots along the stage-2 L1 trajectory. After fitting stage 2 as it is now (400 rounds continued from the 200-round L2 warm start), predict the test set at cumulative round counts 300, 400, 500 and 600 by calling the booster with iteration_range=(0, k) for each k (use xgboost.DMatrix or the sklearn wrapper's iteration_range argument), with stage 2 extended to 600 rounds so all snapshots exist. Average those four prediction vectors and add the ridge base. Keep features, ridge base and all tree hyperparameters as they are. Boosted MAE models tend to oscillate late in training because the L1 gradient is a sign, so averaging nearby snapshots should cut that oscillation at essentially no extra cost.
backlog.title: Snapshot averaging over the tail of the L1 stage

backlog.spec: Caco-2 log-permeability values have a long low tail that an MAE objective handles but a squared-error warm-start stage does not. Before fitting, clip the training target to its 2nd and 98th training percentiles and use the clipped values everywhere the booster and the Ridge baseline are fitted. Do not clip the returned predictions. Keep the feature matrix, the two-stage structure and all hyperparameters unchanged. This limits how far a handful of extreme molecules can drag the early squared-error rounds.
backlog.title: Winsorize the target and train the booster on the clipped scale

backlog.spec: The current Ridge baseline is fit on the full training set and then subtracted from the same rows, so the residuals the booster learns are optimistically small and mismatched with test-time residuals. Change it to an out-of-fold baseline: use sklearn.model_selection.KFold with 10 splits shuffled by seed on the scaled physchem matrix, fill base_tr with out-of-fold Ridge predictions, and compute base_te from a Ridge refit on all training rows. The booster then trains on honest residuals. Keep alpha=1.0, the descriptor set, the feature matrix and all boosting hyperparameters as they are.
backlog.title: Replace the Ridge baseline with a cross-fitted linear baseline

backlog.spec: Keep the Ridge baseline on physchem descriptors and the feature matrix exactly as they are. Change only the residual model: instead of one two-stage XGBoost fit, run the same two-stage fit (200 squared-error trees then 400 absolute-error trees continuing from the first booster) five times with random_state set to seed, seed+1, seed+2, seed+3, seed+4, and return base_te plus the arithmetic mean of the five stage-2 test predictions. This averages away variance coming from subsample=0.8 and colsample_bytree=0.3. Runtime grows roughly fivefold but should stay well inside the limit.
backlog.title: Seed-bag the gradient boosting residual model

backlog.spec: Keep the architecture and the two-stage schedule but regularize the trees harder, since 728 rows with roughly 2200 features is a strongly over-parameterized setting. Change the shared XGBoost parameters to max_depth=4, min_child_weight=6, reg_lambda=5.0, gamma=0.5, subsample=0.7, colsample_bytree=0.2, colsample_bylevel=0.7, learning_rate=0.03, and compensate for the shallower trees by using 300 stage-1 squared-error rounds and 700 stage-2 absoluteerror rounds continued from stage 1. The physchem ridge base, the features and the overall two-stage structure stay exactly as they are. The hypothesis is that the current depth-6 trees with min_child_weight=3 can isolate individual scaffolds, which hurts on folds that test on unseen skeletons.
backlog.title: Stronger leaf and split regularization in XGBoost

memo: Helped: swapping RF for XGBoost with L1 loss (0.3828, -0.0589 vs the 0.4417 start). Adding a ridge on six RDKit physchem descriptors plus aromatic-atom features, with XGB fitting its residuals, gave 0.3755/0.3715. A two-stage XGB residual fit (200 rounds of squared-error, then L1) is the current incumbent at 0.3658/0.3652 over 2 runs. Noise-level or no gain (noise sd about 0.0037): bagged XGB 0.3793, 6-model ensemble 0.3795, winsorized targets 0.3727, Avalon+ErG 0.3710, LightGBM, CatBoost, GP, MLP, Tanimoto kernel ridge, MACCS, 3D shape, calibration, quantile correction, polynomial or sparse-L1 ridge bases. Tree and Morgan tuning looks saturated. Next: vary the two-stage recipe (round counts, learning rate, Huber loss for stage two), combine small gains with it (bagging, Avalon/ErG, winsorizing), and add polarity/ionization descriptors (TPSA, HBD, charge) to the ridge. Avoid specs that abort at the engine.
